title: Rufino Tamayo's birth chart
metaDescription: Rufino Tamayo's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 3.3° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 18.6° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 3.3° Virgo — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mercury. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Virgo and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Leo (21.3°), Venus in Leo (27.7°), Mars in Libra (13.2°): a mind that decides at speaking speed, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Saturn to Pluto, a opposition with 0.5° of slack. Across the wheel, each body sees the other in full. The old reading is not conflict so much as permanent mutual visibility. Behind it, the Sun square Uranus at 0.8°, and Venus sextile Neptune at 1.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. The Moon in Taurus at 18.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Libra at 13.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: fire 4, air 3, earth 2, water 1 across the elements, and mutable 5, fixed 4, cardinal 1 across the modalities. Mercury was retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.2° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 18.6°.
